subject: Energy
title: Tokamaks and Stellarators
description: A fast breakdown of Tokamaks and Stellarators for builders.

hook.text: Tokamaks use powerful magnets to confine plasma in a donut shape—trapping hydrogen at 150 million °C for fusion.

buildup.text: ITER, the world's largest tokamak, is under construction in France—a $25 billion international megaproject.

discovery.text: Stellarators twist the donut into a complex shape—harder to build but potentially more stable for continuous operation.

twist.text: Germany's Wendelstein 7-X stellarator achieved record plasma confinement in 2023—proving the concept works.

climax.text: Neither approach has produced net electricity yet—ITER aims for first fusion power by the mid-2030s.

punchline.text: Trap plasma in magnets—two paths to the same burning star.

quiz.question: Where is the ITER tokamak being built?
